name: Depreciation — Schedule II to the Companies Act, 2013
definition: Depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life. The depreciable amount is the cost of the asset, or the other amount substituted for cost, less its residual value. The useful life is the period over which the asset is expected to be available for use by an entity, or the number of production or similar units expected to be obtained from it. For the purposes of Schedule II, depreciation includes amortisation.
why_it_exists: Schedule II is headed '(See section 123)', and s.123(2) requires that depreciation be provided in accordance with Schedule II for the profits out of which dividend is declared. It replaces a free choice of write-off with a specified useful life per class of asset and a cap on residual value, so that reported profit cannot be manufactured by stretching an asset's life.
inputs: the cost of the asset, or the other amount substituted for cost
the residual value of the asset
the useful life of the asset, from Part C or a justified alternative
the date of any addition, sale, discard, demolition or destruction during the financial year
the number of shifts the asset was worked
outputs: the depreciation charge for the financial year
disclosure of the depreciation methods used, and of useful lives where they differ from the Schedule
preconditions: the entity is a company to which the Companies Act, 2013 applies
the asset is a tangible asset within Part C, or an intangible asset for which paragraph 3(ii) routes to the Accounting Standards
exceptions: Part B, paragraph 4 — a useful life or residual value notified for accounting purposes by a Regulatory Authority constituted under an Act of Parliament, or by the Central Government, is applied irrespective of the requirements of Schedule II
paragraph 3(i) proviso — a company may adopt a different useful life or residual value if the financial statements disclose the difference and provide justification duly supported by technical advice
Note 6 — assets marked NESD in Part C get no extra shift depreciation
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as enacted 2013; amendments not held locally

Beyond the general amendment caveat: Schedule II as printed in this source is NOT purely the 2013 text. Paragraph 3(i) and paragraph 4 each carry a footnote recording substitution by Notification G.S.R. 627(E) dated 29 August 2014.
common_mistakes: reading Part C as a table of depreciation RATES — paragraph 5 introduces it as the useful lives of various tangible assets
leaving a residual value above five per cent. of original cost with no disclosure and no technical justification
charging a full year's depreciation on an asset added or disposed of mid-year — Note 2 requires a pro rata basis
applying a Schedule II life where a Regulatory Authority has notified one — Part B paragraph 4 overrides
assuming the printed Schedule is the enacted 2013 text — paragraphs 3(i) and 4 were substituted in 2014
icai_references: Schedule II paragraph 3(ii), as printed, routes intangible assets to the relevant Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), or to the Accounting Standards under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2006 where Ind AS does not apply. That paragraph is itself substituted text and the standards are not held in this source.
UNKNOWN — no ICAI standard on depreciation is extracted here
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — whether depreciation may be claimed on the tax component of a capital good is a separate question under the CGST Act and is not decided by Schedule II
evidence_required: cost of the asset, or the other amount substituted for cost
residual value, and the technical advice where it exceeds five per cent. of original cost
date of addition, or of sale, discard, demolition or destruction
the useful life applied, and the justification where it differs from Part C
any Regulatory Authority notification of a useful life or residual value for the asset
confidence_factors: weak when the asset class cannot be matched to a Part C line — the useful life is then unresolved
weak when the acquisition or disposal date is missing — the Note 2 pro rata computation cannot be performed
weak for an intangible asset — paragraph 3(ii) routes it out of Schedule II to the Accounting Standards, which are not held here

UNKNOWN — the depreciation METHOD (straight line, written down value, unit of production) is not specified in the Schedule II text extracted here; Note 3(i) only requires the methods used to be disclosed
validation_checks: residual value does not exceed five per cent. of the original cost, or the difference is disclosed with justification duly supported by technical advice
the useful life applied matches Part C, or the difference is disclosed with justification duly supported by technical advice
an asset added or disposed of during the year is depreciated pro rata from or up to that date
the depreciation methods used are disclosed in the accounts
any Regulatory Authority notified useful life or residual value has been applied in preference to the Schedule
examples: a building other than a factory building, RCC frame structure — useful life 60 years, Part C item I(a)
an end user device such as a desktop or laptop — useful life 3 years, Part C item XII(ii)
office equipment, marked NESD — useful life 5 years, and no extra shift depreciation
counterexamples: an asset whose useful life a Regulatory Authority constituted under an Act of Parliament has notified — Schedule II does not decide it
a residual value set at ten per cent. of original cost with nothing disclosed — outside paragraph 3(i) and its proviso

evidence.quote: SCHEDULE II (See section 123) USEFUL LIVES TO COMPUTE DEPRECIATION
For the purposes of clause (a) of sub-section (1), depreciation shall be provided in accordance with the provisions of Schedule II
Depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life
The depreciable amount of an asset is the cost of an asset or other amount substituted for cost, less its residual value

The useful life of an asset is the period over which an asset is expected to be available for use by an entity, or the number of production or similar units expected to be obtained from the asset by the entity
For the purpose of this Schedule, the term depreciation includes amortisation

The useful life of an asset shall not ordinarily be different from the useful life specified in Part C and the residual value of an asset shall not be more than five per cent. of the original cost of the asset

evidence.section: Schedule II, Part A, paragraph 3(i), proviso
evidence.quote: where a company adopts a useful life different from what is specified in Part C or uses a residual value different from the limit specified above, the financial statements shall disclose such difference and provide justification in this behalf duly supported by technical advice

The useful life or residual value of any specific asset, as notified for accounting purposes by a Regulatory Authority constituted under an Act of Parliament or by the Central Government shall be applied in calculating the depreciation to be provided for such asset irrespective of the requirements of this Schedule
Subject to Parts A and B above, the following are the useful lives of various tangible assets
